prompt_en: Photorealistic cinematic Stonepunk environmental portrait inside a tidal observatory carved from colossal concentric basalt rings above a rough sea. An unmistakably adult woman, using Image 1 only as appearance guidance, has long near-black wavy hair, warm brown almond-shaped eyes, softly arched brows, a slim oval face, and natural rose lips. She wears a black woven-flax mantle armored with overlapping polished-shale plates and stone fasteners. At blue hour she locks a fist-sized quartz chronometer into a hand-cranked stone astrolabe. Her left hand braces the crystal socket while her right turns a carved granite crank. Dominant fitted basalt forms a readable working system of dark wood axles, pale bone lever tips, taut rawhide lashings, and braided plant-fiber tension lines. Interlocking basalt gears bite into a grooved circular stone track while a dark wooden axle turns inside visibly worn stone bearings. A counterweighted monolith arm is visibly linked to that gear train. Quartz veins continue from the seated chronometer through the mechanism into luminous tide-line carvings. Beside the socket, a carved slate diagnostic board aligns four mineral pegs with fiber gauges for axle position, lashing tension, bearing wear, and ring travel; each gauge line visibly reaches its measured part. A replacement rawhide lashing rests in a grooved shale handoff cradle while a small stone counterweight visibly supports the load. Multiple fitted outer rings carry carved channels and raised measurement marks; one ring has shifted open and a breaking wave throws spray through the aperture. Use a medium-wide three-quarter frame and 40 mm deep focus so her face, both hands, the wearables, every prop, the complete mechanical path, and the opened sea aperture remain readable. Blue-hour skylight and quartz glow share reflections across skin, flax, shale, wood, bone, and wet basalt.
